subject.title: feat(sandbox): route plugin-tool untrusted fetch+extract through Docker sandbox

question: Should OpenClaw publish `sandboxed-fetch-runtime` as a supported generic plugin SDK contract now, or keep this capability private/plugin-local until its long-term sandbox API and additional consumers are approved?
rationale: The diff adds a permanent external SDK entrypoint and trusted runtime context field; repository policy treats such boundaries as deliberate contracts, and the provided review history contains no maintainer approval resolving that API direction.

options.title: Approve a narrow public contract
options.body: Approve the SDK subpath after the fail-closed repair and document the supported bridge lifecycle, caller contract, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Keep it plugin-local for now
options.body: Avoid publishing the new SDK subpath and use a private owner-plugin integration until maintainers select a broader sandbox capability seam.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the PR if sandboxed plugin processing is not a core-supported extension direction at this time.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow public contract
recommendation.body: Approve the SDK subpath after the fail-closed repair and document the supported bridge lifecycle, caller contract, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the public core/plugin SDK boundary rather than a mechanical sandbox fix alone.
